newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian mayor and two candidates kidnapped.
newsitem.headline: Colombian mayor and two candidates kidnapped.

text.p: The mayor and two mayoral candidates of a small town in northwest Colombia were kidnapped over the weekend, adding to the violent run up to October's local elections, local media reported on Monday.
Raul Roldan, mayor of Yali, was kidnapped on Saturday by two men who said they were acting on orders from leftist rebel commanders, Medellin's El Colombiano newspaper said.
"They said they needed to talk with the mayor about political matters," a government official who witnessed the kidnapping told the daily.
In a separate incident, two Yali mayoral candidates agreed to meet with members of a "subversive group" on Saturday night and have not been heard from since, the newspaper reported.

Colombians will go to the polls in October to elect town mayors -- offices that have become extremely dangerous as armed groups on both ends of the political spectrum exert increasing influence in large regions of the country.

Colombia's left-wing guerrilla groups have said they will not allow political campaigning in areas under their control. And right-wing paramilitary groups have sworn in recent months to kill mayoral candidates who oppose their political views. At least six mayors have been killed so far this year, and more than 20 have been killed since January 1996.

Earlier this month, the state insurance agency La Previsora S.A. announced a new insurance policy to cover medical and funeral expenses of political candidates injured and killed during the campaign season.
